selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer tracks health and values science-backed outcomes, perfectly matching the advertiser's focus on adaptogens and functional beverages. She can be reached on Daily Form.
The Gen Z Aesthete is drawn to functional beverages and visual brand identity, aligning with the advertiser's trendy cocktail alternative concept. She can be reached on Pop & Sip.

The Fitness Enthusiast looks for recovery and functional beverages to support an active lifestyle, fitting the advertiser's non-alcoholic and feel-good value proposition. He can be reached on Pop & Sip.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent prioritizes bulk buying and family-friendly household products, which does not match a single-item functional beverage advertiser.
The Pet Parent focuses strictly on pet supplies and pet health, making human beverages irrelevant to their purchasing habits.
The Affluent Classic prefers traditional home goods, luxury apparel, and heritage brands rather than trendy functional beverage alternatives.
The Sustainability Buyer focuses on supply chain transparency and eco-certifications for apparel and home goods rather than beverage-specific functional benefits.
The Convenience-First Millennial relies on instant grocery delivery and quick commerce apps rather than the DTC wellness publishers recommended here.
The Value-Conscious Shopper seeks heavy discounts and bundle deals, clashing with the mid-tier $40 AOV pricing of this specialty drink.
The Gifter buys premium items specifically for gifting holidays and explicitly dislikes subscription-only or self-care framing, missing the everyday functional beverage use case.
